text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NEWS
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said some foreign countries are funding organisations involved in terrorism in Pakistan.
- Justice Saiduzzam Siddiqui was sworn in as acting chief justice.
THE MUSLIM
- The government plans to build a port at Gwadar and complete a major part of work in the current financial year.
DAWN
- The state's Privatisation Commission has finalised a plan to disinvest all the state-run commercial banks and financial institutions by March 1998, sources said.
- Three alleged bandits were shot dead and one of their accomplices arrested in a gunbattle with police in Karachi.
- More then 500 people were arrested in Karachi as police stepped up their campaign to find the killers of Shahid Hamid, chief of the state-run Karachi Electric Supply Corporation.
- State-run Pakistan International Airlines will raise domestic fares by 10 percent on select routes from July 15.
- A Shi'ite Moslem religious scholar was killed in sectarian violence in Lahore.
- The paramilitary Frontier Constabulary will replace police at all sensitive places and security will be beefed up at key installations in Islamabad.
- A 22-year-old man was torn to pieces and six were wounded in an explosion in a slum in the Liaquatabad area of Karachi.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said Pakistan would not default on debt repayments due in the next few weeks.
- A high-level Indian delegation will visit Pakistan soon to explore possibilities of buying electricity from Islamabad to end India's chronic power shortage, an official said in New Delhi.
- The government has decided to invite fresh tenders for the construction of storage/liquefied petroleum gas terminal and related infrastructure development at Karachi's Port Qasim.

- The private Muslim Commercial Bank said it will reduce interest rates charged on loans by around one percent within a couple of days in line with government policy of ensuring cheaper credit for the different sectors of the economy.
- The Board of Investment proposed duty-free import of components for the local manufacture of bulldozers and excavators.
- The Privatisation Commission handed over 70 percent of the shares and management control of Habib Credit and Exchange Bank Ltd to Nahyan Bin Mubarak al-Nahyan consortium of Abu Dhabi.
- ANZ Grindlays Bank has arranged and underwritten a $30 million revolving letter of credit and financing facility for the state-run Pakistan State Oil to facilitate oil imports.
- BUSINESS RECORDER
- Farmers attending a meeting from all over the country unanimously decided not to pay agriculture tax saying that the tax was on land-holding rather than agricultural income.

- The World Bank has warned the government that if Provincial Irrigation Development Authorities are not set up by July 31, the credit of $785 million for the National Drainage Programme will not be released.
- The Finance Ministry has invited nine parties to present proposals to raise $500 million from securitisation of expatriate workers remittances.
FINANCIAL POST
- Pakistan is poised to negotiate a $1.5 billion loan agreement with the International Monetary Fund mission scheduled to arrive this week.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
